And Iudas al{{ls}}o that betraied him, {{ls}}toode vvith them. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=6}} As {{ls}}one therfore as he {{ls}}aid to them, I am he: they vvent backvvard, and fel to the ground. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=7}} Againe therfore he a{{ls}}ked them, VVhom {{ls}}eeke ye? And they {{ls}}aid, {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=8}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, I haue told you, that I am he. if therfore you {{ls}}eeke me, let the{{ls}}e goe their vvaies. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=9}} That the vvord might be fulfilled vvhich he {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 17, 12.''}}* That of them vvhom thou ha{{ls}}t giuen me, I haue not lo{{ls}}t any. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=10}} Simon Peter therfore hauing a {{ls}}vvord, drevve it out: and {{ls}}mote the {{ls}}eruant of the high prie{{ls}}t: & cut of his right eare. And the name of the {{ls}}eruant vvas Malchus. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=11}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aid to Peter, Put vp thy {{ls}}vvord into the {{ls}}cabbard. The chalice vvhich my father hath giuen me, {{ls}}hal not I drinke it? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=12}} The band therfore and the Tribune & the mini{{ls}}ters of the Ievves apprehended {{sc|Iesvs}}, and bound him: {{verse|chapter=18|verse=13}} and they brought him to Annas fir{{ls}}t, for he vvas father in lavv to Caiphas, vvho vvas the high prie{{ls}}t of that yere. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=14}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 11, 49.''}}* Caiphas vvas he that had giuen the coun{{ls}}el to the Ievves, That it is expedient that one man die for the people.
